correctness.rationale: For r>=2, every flat disjunct must avoid both output values for the same predictor tuple, because such a pair is an inconsistent two-team. Extend its partial graph to a total Boolean function. Every consistent s-team, s=min(r,2^k), forces one row to reproduce each s-subset assignment, the exact covering-array requirement. Conversely any array gives full-graph classical formulas and covers all consistent smaller teams by extending each partial labeling to s input positions. Invalid teams cannot lie in a graph. At r=1 the tautology is valid. At r>=2^k, all 2^(2^k) total output graphs must appear; strength-two exact minimum and asymptotic are taken from Lawrence et al. The standalone checker exhaustively verifies illustrative small arrays and all bounded teams for k=1,2. No finite testing substitutes for the universal proof.

value.rationale: The cardinality restriction is intrinsic to team semantics (finite information states). The theorem identifies the exact number of truth-conditional alternatives needed to express one functional-dependence assertion under every team-size budget, giving a sharp transition from the trivial singleton case to a pairwise-covering optimum of order k, then to 2^(2^k) full dependence functions. It connects logical resource measurement with an independently developed combinatorial design optimization problem for every strength, providing usable bounds and constructions. No claim is made about arbitrary formula size or solving higher-strength covering-array tables.
